convoLines.text: "Do you dream about before? Or is it all — this — now? Happy?"
"Then it's not gone. Not really. Keep going back."
The ground remembers.
Names, named.
You watch who eats with whom, who laughs a little too loud at whose jokes. Nothing solid. Keep looking.
The moot is called. The fire gets built up.
"Okay, that's my quota of socializing."
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"What's the kindest thing someone's done for you out here?"
"That's the good stuff. Quiet generosity. It's holding this whole thing together."
Another pass over the same ground. Somebody's being careful. Careful people leave cleaner trails — and cleaner trails are still trails.
You say nothing. The silence sits at the fire with everyone else.
The moot is called. The fire gets built up.
Counted.
"Anyway — I should get back to it. Good talking, though."
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Can we talk?" Lucas sits down near you. "Just... talk. Like people used to."
"Hah. I'm not okay. I'm saying it out loud so it's real: I'm not okay."
"Good. Company's company."
"I keep going over it. Having someone here... it slows the spiral. Anyway."
"Still on that hard time."
Their voice loosens. The guardedness thins.
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Alright, duty calls. This was a good pause."
"You're a good listener, you know that?" A tired smile.
"Thanks for... you know. Just listening."
"I keep expecting to see them by the fire. Then I remember."
"Walk with me? I want another pair of eyes on something."
You walk to the tree line with Aki. Nothing much there — but they talk the whole way, and you learn the shape of them a little better.
"I — yeah. It helps, hearing that."
"Aubrey always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"I've got things to do. People to avoid. You know."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"We never finished talking about what's been happening — we left it mid-thought, 7 days back. 'You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.'"
"Walk with me? I want another pair of eyes on something."
Aki shows you where they go to think. "Don't tell the others. Everyone needs one place."
"There's more, but that's for another fire."
"I rinse the cup twice when the fire gets loud. Everyone's got a tell. That's mine."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on what's been happening."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Right. Done. Don't look so relieved."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"This was good." They mean it.
"Can I tell you something? I saw something in the woods I'm not telling anyone about."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on their secret."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
You show them Groundnut — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"Don't tell anyone I told you. What's on your mind?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "You feel that? The air before a storm. That's the village right now."
"I stay out of it. Mostly. It's getting harder."
"I've got things to see to. Don't be a stranger."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"I tried the Groundnut like you showed me. Didn't poison anyone, so that's a win."
"Come get air with me. I need to think out loud."
You walk to the ridge with Lucas. Nothing much there — but they talk the whole way, and you learn the shape of them a little better.
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on that plant lesson."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"Yeah? What's up?"

"Good question." "Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "Have you heard what they're calling Drum-Belly? Michelle is pushing 'The Ugly Beast'. Everyone's got a name for it and nobody agrees."
"All right. Thank you for telling me."
"My part? I hum one note, over and over, when the dark comes and stay neutral until there's a winner."
"Right. Go on, then."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Between us — What do you miss most? From before."
"God. Yes. I dream about soup. Actual soup, with a spoon."
"Hot showers. Not the big things — the small, stupid, perfect things. Columbus, Ohio in the morning, coffee going, nobody trying to kill me. I miss being bored."
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"Still on what you miss most. Seen worse."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want? Just... be straight with me."
"We went over this," Michelle says, a little tired. "I already told you the truth about that."
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"You told me about people sharing food they couldn't spare. Quiet. No performance. Seen it again since?"
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Look — Still on that personal stuff."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Last time things were different. They always are." "Everyone's choosing sides and pretending they aren't. I hate it."
"That's... pretty much all of it, honestly."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"You missed a real hot meal. Soup, you said — with a spoon. Any of that turn up?"
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Yeah? What's up? Not that it matters."
"Permit me: Still on that personal stuff."
Something crosses their face — quick, then gone. The practiced expression clicks back into place.
"Oh." A long pause. "I don't actually want to survive, whatever it takes. I want to belong somewhere. It's safer if people don't know. Please don't tell the others." Michelle won't meet your eyes.
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
"Right. Go on, then."
